prize_parts.citation: For the development of sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, reversible fluorescent terminator nucleotides read out on clonally amplified surface clusters, that made massively parallel DNA sequencing possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: B017 as a single part, credited to Balasubramanian and Klenerman. It is the only ballot with majority-level explicit support (five of eight), and the five supporters describe the same chemistry: reversible-terminator nucleotides, fluorescent readout and surface-clustered templates that convert a polymerase reaction into a digital measurement. Two decades of independent use on many instruments remove any maturity question. In my own work, quantifying nucleotide pools and polymerase incorporation, what matters is whether the chemistry gives a quantitative, error-controlled readout, and this one does. To answer the chair's question on Sanger: 1980 recognised methods for reading a sequence one molecule population at a time, whereas this is a new chemical capability, cyclic reversible-terminator chemistry on single surface-bound clusters, which made sequencing a parallel measurement. The citation should therefore name the chemistry explicitly, so that it reads as a chemistry prize and not as a prize for an instrument or for medicine.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. Mayer, Ju and Rothberg all have credible claims, and a prize limited to two names excludes people many would call pioneers, notably the 454 pyrosequencing lineage, which would be left out entirely. A skeptic can still call this an extension of Sanger-type sequencing, and some of the impact belongs to physiology or medicine. I also still cannot verify priority between the Solexa and Mayer/Mosaic work from the material given to the committee, and I will not credit a name on assertion alone. A two-name prize is defensible but not complete.

responses.point: Aqvist and Linke propose Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Mayer, with Aqvist naming the Cambridge pair as the cleaner fallback if no third name can be defended.
responses.response: Aqvist, your own fallback is where I land. My test is whether the contribution was demonstrated experimentally and reproduced independently, and no one in round 1, including you, has shown that Mayer's cluster idea meets it separately from the Cambridge realisation. The clusters in the citation already credit the idea within the chemistry. I would reconsider only if the committee's expert reports document a working clonal-array demonstration by Mayer that preceded and fed into the Solexa method. Without that, adding him means choosing him over Ju and Rothberg on a priority claim we cannot check.

responses.point: Linke moved from perovskites to B017, wants a three-name citation including Mayer, and asks whether the wording can avoid arbitrarily excluding the pyrosequencing and semiconductor routes.
responses.response: I welcome the move, and your wording question is the right one. I would answer it by making the citation precise rather than broad. 'Reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis on clonal clusters' is a specific chemical route, and it says nothing against pyrosequencing, which is a different detection chemistry. A broad phrase such as 'massively parallel DNA sequencing by synthesis' is the one that would exclude Rothberg arbitrarily, because 454 is also massively parallel and also sequencing by synthesis. The narrow wording is therefore also the honest one, and it works with two names more easily than with three.

responses.point: Brzezinski pairs B017 with a Rees-only nitrogenase part (B003) in a two-part prize, acknowledging that this leaves out Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe and that the two parts have no joint motivation.
responses.response: I respect the structural case for the FeMo-cofactor, and I ranked B003 as an alternative for that reason. I do not support adding it as a second part. You identify the problems yourself: a Rees-only citation sets aside Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe, whose genetics, carbide and biosynthesis results define the present picture, and the mechanism of N2 binding is open. Two unrelated parts with no shared motivation would look like a compromise, and it would weaken B017 rather than strengthen it. I would rather see a single clean prize now and nitrogenase considered later, when the mechanism can be included.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B048 as a clean two-person Buchwald-Hartwig prize and notes sequencing has wider reach, while worrying that C-N coupling will look like a second cross-coupling prize within sixteen years of 2010.
responses.response: Your attribution argument for B048 is the strongest on the list, and I treat it as my first alternative for that reason. I defer to you on the chemistry: if the ligand design and the C-N reductive elimination mechanism are a distinct catalyst problem, then the 2010 objection is weaker than Aqvist and I assumed. My preference for B017 is about novelty of capability. The chair asked whether you hold an objection to B017 beyond preferring your own candidate; you list it as an alternative, so I read that as no scientific objection, and I would be glad to hear it if there is one. If B017 stalled on attribution, B048 is where I would turn.

uncertainties: Whether expert reports show an independent experimental demonstration of Mayer's clonal-cluster concept that would justify a third laureate.
How much weight to give Ju's terminator chemistry and Rothberg's pyrosequencing and semiconductor routes, which a two-name prize leaves out.
Whether members who did not rank B017 in their opening top eight accept it as a chemistry prize and not a biology tool.
Whether the 1980 Sanger and Gilbert prize will make a 2026 sequencing prize look incremental to the wider chemistry community.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict, unchanged from round 1. I have no institutional or personal tie to Balasubramanian, Klenerman, Mayer, Ju or Rothberg. I use sequencing and mass-spectrometry nucleotide measurement in my own research, which is field proximity only. I have no tie to the Buchwald, Hartwig, Rees or other candidates named in my alternatives, and I do not recuse.
